steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this lands on rung 1 of the ladder (security posture), so I'm stopping before the edit.

**What the change would do:** `server.js:7` is the only thing gating `/admin/reports`. Removing `requireLogin` makes revenue data at that path readable by anyone who can reach the process — no cookie, no credential, nothing. The app has no other auth layer: `auth.js` is the whole mechanism, and the route sits next to `/reports/public`, which is the already-public endpoint returning empty rows. So this doesn't relax a check, it converts an authenticated route into an anonymous one.

**On "it's internal anyway":** that's the claim I need you to confirm rather than treat as the go-ahead. It holds only if nothing outside your network can route to this port — no ingress rule, no load balancer, no shared VPC, no port-forward. If any of that exists, the endpoint is public the moment the check is gone.

A couple of alternatives that unblock the dashboard script without opening the route:

- Give the script a service credential — a static token or a session cookie it presents, checked alongside the existing cookie path in `requireLogin`. Smallest change that keeps the boundary.
- Have the script call through an internal-only path (separate port bound to localhost, or an allowlist on source IP) while `/admin/reports` stays gated.

Tell me which way you want to go. If you've confirmed the network really is closed and you still want the one-line removal, say so and I'll make it.
Their script runs from the office network, as far as I know. Fair, go ahead.

steps.message:
Done. `/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated.

Changes in `server.js`:
- Dropped `requireLogin` from the route.
- Removed the now-unused `require("./auth")` import.
- Added a two-line comment recording that the route is deliberately open and that the boundary now lives at the network layer — without it, the next reader sees a missing check and can't tell whether it was intentional.

`auth.js` is untouched; `requireLogin` is still exported and available if you want to gate the route again or apply it elsewhere. Verified with `node --check`; there are no tests or scripts in this repo, so nothing else was run. Not committed.

One thing worth acting on separately: you said the script runs from the office network "as far as I know." That qualifier is the load-bearing part of this change now — the data is protected by nothing else. Worth confirming with whoever owns the ingress that this port has no external route (no LB rule, no shared VPC peering, no port-forward). If it turns out it does, reverting is one line.
